witnesses.provenance: Solana's per-transaction MAX_COMPUTE_UNIT_LIMIT is 1,400,000 compute units. It is the chain's limit, not ours. The campaigns set ProgramTest's ceiling to exactly that value and never raise it, so a transaction that did not fit would fail rather than be re-run with headroom.

witnesses.query: .transactions[] | select(.label == "claims position: admit") | [.logs[] | select(startswith("Program return: CxeKLJRofna6h2GqCsjdVwc2D7EdDFX8uDy9KGw3Ey68 "))] | last | split(" ")[3] | ((length * 3 / 4) - (if endswith("==") then 2 elif endswith("=") then 1 else 0 end)) | tostring
witnesses.provenance: PROTOCOL_POSITION_ADMISSION_BYTES_V2 = 512 (crates/dclutch-claims-svm/src/protocol_position_v2.rs:15) is the exact backward receipt dependency the sparse composition requires (commit 78bda05). This checks it against a SECOND, independent derivation: the base64 the RUNTIME wrote into the transaction's own `Program return:` log line, decoded by length arithmetic here rather than by any dClutch code.

witnesses.query: .transactions[] | select(.label == "claims sparse: admit, transfer and close") | [.logs[] | select(startswith("Program return: CxeKLJRofna6h2GqCsjdVwc2D7EdDFX8uDy9KGw3Ey68 ")) | split(" ")[3] | (length * 3 / 4) - (if endswith("==") then 2 elif endswith("=") then 1 else 0 end)] | tostring
witnesses.provenance: The composition of commit 78bda05 is keyed on three exact receipt widths: PROTOCOL_POSITION_ADMISSION_BYTES_V2 = 512, SPARSE_NATIVE_TRANSFER_RECEIPT_BYTES_V1 = 448 and PROTOCOL_POSITION_CLOSE_RECEIPT_BYTES_V2 = 416 (crates/dclutch-claims-svm/src/{protocol_position_v2,sparse_native_transfer_v1}.rs). This checks all three, IN ORDER, against a second and independent derivation: the base64 the RUNTIME wrote into the transaction's own `Program return:` lines, decoded by length arithmetic here rather than by any dClutch code. A stage that stopped running, or one whose receipt changed width, moves this list.

witnesses.query: .transactions[] | select(.label == "claims sparse: admit, transfer and close") | [.logs[] | select(. == "Program CxeKLJRofna6h2GqCsjdVwc2D7EdDFX8uDy9KGw3Ey68 success")] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: The runtime writes `Program <address> success` once per returning invocation. Three of them inside one transaction is the chain's own account of Admit -> SparseNativeTransfer -> Close, and it is what distinguishes an executed composition from a campaign that merely submitted one instruction.

witnesses.query: .transactions[] | select(.label == "claims sparse: caller refuses after the complete chain") | (if .error == null then "committed" else ([.logs[] | select(. == "Program CxeKLJRofna6h2GqCsjdVwc2D7EdDFX8uDy9KGw3Ey68 success")] | length | tostring) end)
witnesses.provenance: A rollback case is only evidence if the thing being rolled back actually happened. This asserts, from the runtime's own log, that a transaction the ledger records as FAILED contains three completed Claims invocations. The `if .error == null` guard makes a campaign that accidentally let the transaction commit fail this witness rather than pass it.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.error != null) | select([.logs[] | select(contains("custom program error: 0x"))] | length == 0)] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: The Solana runtime reports a privilege, frame, or account refusal it decides ITSELF as a bare InstructionError with no `custom program error:` log line; that line appears only when a program returned ProgramError::Custom. Every refusal this campaign claims is a program decision, so a bare runtime refusal appearing here would mean a hostile case stopped being about the program.
